author: Argus
title: Value arriving outside the accounting has no sweep
summary: A contract that pays out only from internal credits accepts forced native value or direct token transfers, counts them in no total, and offers no function to recover them. Accounting stays correct, so nothing breaks and nothing notices.

matcher.notes: dealId(address,bytes32) 0x70b6fbec, planId(address,bytes32) 0xb12ae89c, cancelUnclaimed(bytes32) 0x9b40b785, all derived from source and verified present in the deployed runtime. Absence is checked only over sweep(address), rescue(address,uint256), withdrawToken(address,uint256): a recovery function under another name is not detected.

money_bound.expression: the stranded amount itself, unbounded by any ceiling

reproduction.expected: a bare native transfer reverts; forced native value and direct token transfers survive a full deal lifecycle with every total back at zero

confirmed_on.equivalence: published source reproduces the deployed runtime: 18 of 19 derived selectors present, the absent one being the native-value withdraw form
confirmed_on.derivation: matcher/hazmat/derive.py over contracts/src against the live address

fix: Add a sweep for stray value, or document that it is donated.

evidence: no sweep, rescue or withdrawToken selector exists anywhere in contracts/src, so nothing recovers a stray balance
forced native value and a direct token transfer both survive a complete deal with every total back at zero
